land.text: Sicily, the island half of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies (the page's location: 'Sicily, Kingdom of the Two Sicilies')

predecessors.note: The Two Sicilies seed lists this row as its only 1848 neighbour; the Two Sicilies ledger records the loss in January 1848.

land.text: the Bourbon army 'retook full control of the island on 15 May 1849 by force'

capitals.name: Palermo
capitals.note: The page names no capital; it says the revolution was centred in Palermo, where the Provisional Government and the Sicilian Parliament sat (a reading).

correction.text: The shape unchanged (Sicily without the Messina corner), held from 12 January 1848 to 15 May 1849: the years run into 1849, Cliopatria's single year does not

keyframe_review.note: 21,788 km2 = 76 grid cells, all inside the gazetteer's Sicily region (89 cells); the 13 missing cells include the Messina corner, which agrees with the page: the Sicilian Parliament 'was never able to control' Messina. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible. Only the years change: the infobox gives 12 January 1848 - 15 May 1849, Cliopatria draws 1848 alone. Cliopatria's Wikipedia field ('Italian nationalism') and Wikidata id (Q6093359) point to the ideology, not to this state.

region.text: Palermo, where 'the substantive acts of the revolution occurred on 12 January 1848'

ledger.note: 12 January 1848: Palermo rises against the Bourbons and the Provisional Government founds the self-proclaimed Kingdom of Sicily. 'the substantive acts of the revolution occurred on 12 January 1848'; the kingdom 'lasted from 12 January 1848 to 15 May 1849'. The page names no separate declaration of independence.

region.text: the island 'broadly' controlled by the revolutionary government, Messina excepted

ledger.note: 1848: the revolution holds the island except Messina. The page: the revolutionary government controlled the island broadly, but the Sicilian Parliament 'was never able to control' Messina, which was well fortified; it does not date the spread, so the month given is the revolution's first.

15 May 1849: the Bourbon army retakes Sicily. The page: it retook 'full control of the island on 15 May 1849 by force'; infobox result 'Revolution suppressed'. The Catania and Palermo dates are not on the page.
15 May 1849: the Sicilian kingdom ends and the island returns to the Two Sicilies (infobox: 12 January 1848 - 15 May 1849).

wars.name: Sicilian revolution of 1848

zones.text: the island; Messina's fortifications held out against the Sicilian Parliament

wars.outcome: The Bourbon army retook the island by force on 15 May 1849; the page's infobox result is 'Revolution suppressed; more powers to the Sicilian local administration' (rebel strength c. 20,000).
wars.note: The page describes a Bourbon bombardment of Messina and a defeat of the regular Sicilian forces there, without a year or month on the part read; no contest zone is drawn for it.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the frontier, but the revolution's hold on the Messina corner was never settled (the page says Parliament was never able to control it), so the north-east edge is soft.

sources.title: Sicilian revolution of 1848
sources.note: Dates (12 January 1848 - 15 May 1849), Ruggero Settimo as effective head of state, Messina never controlled, the Bourbon reconquest. The only page opened for this state (budget 1-2).

notes: WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'Italian Nationalists' (1848 only, 76 cells) is a generic label; its Wikipedia field ('Italian nationalism') and Wikidata id (Q6093359) are the ideology's, so the dossier leaves wikidata null and links the Sicilian revolution page. Identification rests on the geometry (a subset of the gazetteer's Sicily region, Messina's corner missing), the seed (its only neighbour is the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies) and the Two Sicilies dossier of this project, which records the January 1848 loss and the May 1849 recovery against counterpart italian-nationalists. UNSETTLED: the year 1849 has no Cliopatria shape although the state lived to 15 May 1849 (keyframe verdict adjust; the Two Sicilies dossier carries the island back from 1849); Ruggero Settimo's headship is on the page but a ruler strip needs a documented list, so none is given; the page does not say whether a Bourbon garrison held Messina's citadel through 1848; the offer of the crown to a Savoy prince is not on the page. Other 1848-49 Italian risings (Roman Republic of 1849, Republic of San Marco) are separate states handled by other batches.
